text:
deploy-bot: starting blue/green flip APAC -> EU (blueflip v2). target weight APAC: 30%, EU: 70% — rolling over 20s windows. rollout id=rb-2026-03-15-37

alice (deploy): noticed spike in 5xx from APAC canaries ~2 mins in. dashboards show elevated 502s and auth failures.

alice (deploy): logs:```
# apac-canary-1
2026-03-15T10:32:11Z ERROR upstream response 502 from service-auth
2026-03-15T10:32:12Z WARN kv-cache-miss user:abcd token invalid
```

incident-bot: @sre-oncall page (priority: high) — possible region routing instability during rollout. See runbook: <https://console/redwood/runbook/blueflip> :rotating_light:

sre-jay: on it. pulling packet traces + LB weights. can someone confirm if DNS weights were changed before the runtime weights?

alice (deploy): we flipped runtime weights first then pushed DNS weight change 30s later to match. saw clients with old DNS TTL still hitting APAC while platform started shifting to EU -> some requests hit EU backend without expected cookies.

ben (eng-dns): checking DNS logs — ioredns shows high churn for the service FQDN from APAC resolvers. TTL was 30s, many resolvers still honoring old IPs then switching. looks like a splitback loop: clients alternate IPs between APAC and EU causing session auth token mismatch.

paul (platform): that explains the auth invalidation errors. session affinity is IP-based for the legacy auth shard; switching region mid-request invalidates token.

sre-jay: quick mitigation options:
- increase DNS TTL to 300s to stop flapping (but would slow any future rollback)
- abort rollout and roll back runtime weights to original (immediate)
- enable feature flag kill-switch: `blueflip.enabled = false` (fast, safe, runtime-level)

alice (deploy): can we flip the kill-switch now? it reverts new behavior without touching DNS. if flip works we can then roll back DNS.

ben (eng-dns): agree. DNS change takes longer to propagate and is causing the oscillation. please run kill-switch.

sre-jay: executing kill-switch:```
# from opsconsole
POST /flags/blueflip/disable
{ "env": "apac", "force": true }
=> 200 OK, flag_state: disabled
```

sre-jay: monitor shows error rate dropping on APAC canaries within 40s. 502s down from 7% -> 0.8%.

customer-success-liz: we're seeing customer tickets about slow auth and "session expired" from APAC customers on mobile — ETA for fix?

paul (platform): message for CS: immediate mitigation in progress, kill-switch flipped. tell customers we identified a routing/session edge-case during regional rollout and we're stabilizing. will provide update in 30m.

alice (deploy): starting controlled rollback of runtime weights back to pre-rollout values (apac 100% -> apac 100%). rollout id rb-2026-03-15-37 aborted.

deploy-bot: rollback started. rollback id=rb-2026-03-15-37-rollback. progress: node groups 1/6, 2/6...

ben (eng-dns): I'm holding DNS at current state (30s TTL) while we confirm runtime is back to stable. after rollback we should set TTL=300s and remove the DNS change to avoid flapping.

sre-jay: agreed. after rollback, we'll do a small Canary smoke for 10m with kill-switch off in a canary-only env to validate the proper sequence: first DNS, then runtime weights. runbook update required: now recommend changing DNS first for cross-region flows that rely on IP-based affinity.

alice (deploy): noted. also will add a preflight check to detect IP-affinity session types (legacy-auth) and block runtime-first flips if detected.

incident-bot: handoff: @ben (eng-dns) will drive DNS TTL follow-up, @alice (deploy) will own rollout process changes, @sre-jay will own immediate postmortem and metric thresholds.

ben (eng-dns): action item: revert DNS change to previous zone file, set TTL=300s, advise caching teams. will commit in 5m after rollback completes.

paul (platform): action item: add an alert for cross-region session invalidation rate (metric: auth.token.invalidation.count with tag region_mix:true) and create a dashboard panel.

customer-success-liz: messaging note: will post initial customer update in 15m linking to status page and offering direct contacts for impacted enterprise customers.

sre-jay: metrics look stable now. error rate back to baseline. leaving a watch for 45m. creating incident ticket INC-20260315-042 with timeline and initial impact estimate: ~2k requests failed across APAC over 12 minutes, user-facing timeouts for ~0.05% of total traffic.

alice (deploy): post-incident todo: update rollout runbook, add preflight checker, add automated kill-switch run if cross-region token invalidation > 1% in 5m.

ben (eng-dns): follow-up: I'll run a DNS propagation audit and capture resolver behavior to understand which resolvers ignored TTL and bounced.

sre-jay: thanks everyone. tipping point: ordering mismatch (runtime weights before DNS) + low TTL + IP-based session affinity = oscillation loop. will write postmortem and propose changes.

paul (platform): thumbs up. creating a short RCA draft and linking runbook edits.

customer-success-liz: thanks team, keep me posted for the customer note. :thumbsup:

sre-jay: closing chat for now — will reopen if we see any regression.

-- end of thread --
